from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Place a sphere inside the cone.", "It touches the cone at a circle.", "It touches the plane at one point.", "We call this point a focus.", "Dandelin spheres reveal hidden conic geometry."]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        # Visualize circle of contact
        contact_ring = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT).move_to(sphere.get_center())
        self.play(Create(contact_ring))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")

        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")

        self.play(GrowFromCenter(focus_point))

class Section5Scene(ThreeDScene, TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Application", [
            "Dandelin spheres bridge 3D and 2D.",
            "Conics are fundamental geometric properties.",
            "They appear throughout our physical universe."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display final conic section geometry
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=2.5, direction=DOWN).rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT)
        plane = NumberPlane().rotate(PI/6, axis=RIGHT).shift(UP*0.5)
        ellipse = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT).shift(UP*0.5)
        geometry = VGroup(cone, plane, ellipse)
        self.place_in_area(geometry, 'A2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(geometry))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show key measurements, #00FFFF. Label 'a', 'b', 'c'.
        a_label = MathTex("a", color="#00FFFF").next_to(ellipse, RIGHT)
        b_label = MathTex("b", color="#00FFFF").next_to(ellipse, DOWN)
        c_label = MathTex("c", color="#00FFFF").next_to(ellipse, LEFT)
        measurements = VGroup(a_label, b_label, c_label)
        self.play(Write(measurements))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Zoom out to overview
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=-45 * DEGREES, zoom=0.8)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Visualizing Conic Sections
outline.target_audience: High school geometry students or early undergraduates

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of a Cone
sections.content: Define a right circular cone and a cutting plane. Introduce the 'Double Cone' concept to set the stage for all conic types.
sections.example: Imagine a flashlight beam expanding in a dark room; the light forms a cone, and the wall acts as our cutting plane.

sections.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Explain the concept of spheres inscribed within the cone, tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the cutting plane (at a single point). These points of tangency are the 'Foci'.
sections.example: Visualize a marble (sphere) dropped into an ice cream cone until it gets stuck—the circle where it touches the cone is the contact ring.

sections.title: Connecting the Geometry to the Conic
sections.content: Show how the distance from any point on the conic section to the foci relates to the distance to the directrix. Explain that the tangency points of the Dandelin spheres provide the geometric proof for these relationships.
sections.example: A rabbit (the point on the conic) moves such that its distance to a 'carrot' (the focus) and a 'fence' (the directrix) maintains a constant ratio.

sections.title: The Visual Transformation
sections.content: Use a progressive animation: Tilt the plane to transition from a circle (parallel to base) to an ellipse, then a parabola, and finally a hyperbola (parallel to the cone's edge). Show how the Dandelin sphere moves accordingly.
sections.example: An animation of a laser cutter slicing through a 3D model of a cone, changing the angle of the cut to reveal the four conic sections in real-time.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
sections.content: Summarize that Dandelin spheres bridge the gap between 3D solids and 2D curves, proving that conic sections aren't just arbitrary equations but fundamental geometric properties.
sections.example: Satellite orbits (ellipses/hyperbolas) and the physics of how a telescope dish (parabola) focuses starlight to a single point—the focus!
